notes: Rule edit, migrated to the new layout. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is what the scholarship is, stated everywhere, and follows from nothing. No exceptions: the scholarship is tenable only at Oxford (Wikipedia lead). Cambridge: plausible (the other ancient English university) and clearly false. Review fix (main_fix): the well-known members (Bill Clinton, Bob Hawke), their worlds and their indeterminate queries are gone, since README keeps TBox records determinate only, and their by-name worlds denied bridges the record required. All three derived queries now name a fictional new Rhodes Scholar in the prompt, so the rule is the only route (inheritance, 2 hops: the edit and the membership the prompt states); the third is an application (filling a form field). Replaces the earlier 'every pope is the Bishop of Rome' draft, which was dropped for clashing with firm facts about other people. Propositional: negation is worded 'Is it true that it is not the case that ...'; the conjunction's side fact (Newton) is true, the disjunction's (Norway in South America) is false, each with a check. Names were counted in Dolma: none has a hit with 'Oxford' or 'Rhodes'.
